title: As a Deer Pants for Water
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Don't waste your hardship. To get your joy back, stay in the word and prayer, and dig deep into the people of God.
exhortation: Too often we forget how sweet and satisfying God is when we fill ourselves with the things of the world. Television, food, alcohol, scrolling on our phones: they quench and diminish our hunger for God.

We see in this psalm that times of hardship and suffering remind us how much we need God. So often it's in those seasons that we're reminded how wonderful Jesus is: his friendship, his love, his understanding. So my call to myself and to us is this: don't waste your hardship, and don't waste your suffering. Many times we long for the passion for Jesus we had in the past, and when he gives us hardship we ask why. I think it's how we're wired. Sometimes we need it to know how much we need Jesus, and that we can't do things in our own strength.

So how do we get the joy back? We don't go looking for suffering. We start by being in the word and in prayer consistently. But I love how this psalm paints a picture of being with the people of God. Do you want the joy back? Spend time with Christians who are full of joy, who are overflowing with gratitude to God. Find people who are encouraging, older saints who have walked faithfully. Find new converts in your church and invite them over. Nothing fills you with joy like talking with someone who was just saved and is amazed by it. It reminds us what it was like when we were saved.

And when you're with the people of God, don't settle for just being there. Get into it. Talk to people. Seek people out. Ask people to coffee. Have people over and break bread together. If you want the joy back, don't neglect the word, don't neglect pouring your heart out to God in prayer, and don't neglect digging deep into the people of God. There is no better way to remind ourselves of the love of Jesus than to show his love to someone else.
prayer: Lord, may we taste and see that you are good: better than all earthly joys and anything else we could turn to. We need to believe that, Lord. Help our unbelief. Reveal the places in our lives where we don't believe it, places we may be blind to.

May we treasure you above all. May we say with David that, like a deer desperately thirsty for water, we long for you. We long for your word and to commune with you in prayer, not because we have to, but because we earnestly desire it. May that be the cry of our hearts this morning. And may we trust you fully and act on it, because when we exercise our faith we are filled, encouraged and strengthened. May we step out in obedience to you this morning. In Jesus' name, amen.
